item.title: The Longest-Leading Billboard Hot 100 No. 1s
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to this week's music trivia episode. Did you know that only a select few songs have led the Billboard Hot 100 for at least 10 weeks? In fact, just 4% of all Hot 100 No. 1s have achieved this milestone since the chart launched in 1958.
[Short music transition]
Host: Let's take a look at some of these record-breakers. It all started with Debby Boone's "You Light Up My Life" in 1977, which held the top spot for 10 weeks. Olivia Newton-John's "Physical" also reached 10 weeks in 1981-82. But it wasn't until Boyz II Men's "End of the Road" in 1992 that a song dominated for 13 weeks.
[Short music clip from "End of the Road"]
Host: Whitney Houston's "I Will Always Love You" then took the lead, staying at No. 1 for 14 weeks in 1992-93. And in 1995-96, Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men's "One Sweet Day" set a new record with 16 weeks at the top.
[Short music clip from "One Sweet Day"]
Host: This record stood for over 23 years, until Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee's "Despacito" tied it in 2017. And then, Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road" collected 19 weeks at No. 1 in 2019.
[Short music clip from "Old Town Road"]
Host: But the current record-holder is none other than Mariah Carey again, with "All I Want for Christmas Is You" reaching an impressive 22 weeks at No. 1, jingling its way to the top spot every holiday season since 2019.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today's episode. Thanks for joining us on this journey through music history. Tune in next time for more fascinating facts and trivia.
